plan.contextChunk: This figure pairs a coordinate diagram with a magnified inset to define the volume element in spherical coordinates. On the left, x, y, and z axes radiate from a common origin and a small curved orange box floats above the first octant, bounded by two dashed circular arcs of slightly different radii and by dashed rays fanning out from the origin. A bracket on the z axis marks the radial increment Delta rho, the angular gap between the two rays reaching the box is marked Delta phi, and a small angle in the horizontal plane near the origin is marked Delta theta. A flat blue quadrilateral in the xy-plane is the projection of the box, with a bracket beneath labeled rho sin phi and an arrow into it labeled rho sin phi Delta theta. A thick gray curved arrow sweeps right to an enlarged copy of the same box, whose three edges are labeled Delta rho, rho Delta phi, and rho sin phi Delta theta, with Delta V = rho^2 sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta printed below. Showing the subbox in place and again blown up lets each edge be matched to the coordinate increment that generates it. The construction motivates the factor rho^2 sin phi that appears when a triple integral is rewritten in spherical coordinates.

interactions.label: Delta rho

demo_steps.title: The subbox in place
demo_steps.narration: A small spherical wedge sits in the first octant, bounded by shells at rho and rho+Delta rho and by the dashed polar and azimuthal rays. Its horizontal shadow is the blue quad of width rho sin phi.

demo_steps.title: Radial edge = Delta rho
demo_steps.narration: Highlight the radial edge: it is the same length on the curved box and the inset and equals Delta rho with no scaling factor. Drag the Delta rho slider to thicken only this edge.

demo_steps.title: Polar edge = rho Delta phi
demo_steps.narration: Highlight the polar-arc edge. Its physical length is the arc rho Delta phi, so it grows with both rho and Delta phi — an arc length, not a raw angle.

demo_steps.title: Azimuthal edge = rho sin phi Delta theta
demo_steps.narration: Highlight the azimuthal edge and the blue projection. The horizontal circle at polar angle phi has radius rho sin phi, so this edge is rho sin phi Delta theta; multiplying the three edges gives Delta V = rho^2 sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta.

state.edgeHighlight: Azimuthal rho sin phi Delta theta

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World-axis mapping to match the source: world +Y = up = z-axis; world +X = right = y-axis; world +Z = toward viewer / lower-left = x-axis. Axes span ~3 units from origin with arrowheads. Spherical subbox centered at rho=2.0, phi=50deg, theta=30deg; build as a parametric curved wedge (theta in [theta0,theta0+dtheta], phi in [phi0,phi0+dphi], radius in [rho,rho+drho]) with semi-transparent orange faces #e8853a at ~0.55 opacity and darker orange edges #c05a1a. Dashed shell arcs radius 2.0 and 2.0+drho drawn in the box's meridian plane; dashed polar rays from origin to the four box corners; dashed azimuthal rays in the horizontal (world X-Z) plane. z-axis Delta rho bracket at world x~0 spanning the radial thickness projected on z. Blue projection quad #3a5a9a opacity 0.6 lies in the horizontal plane (world Y=0) directly under the box, its width = rho sin phi. Gray sweep arrow #b0b0b0 as a curved tube from the in-place box to the inset. Inset placed at world +X ~ +4.5..+6.5: a straightened box whose three edge lengths are M*drho, M*rho*dphi, M*rho*sin(phi)*dtheta with magnification M~1.4, same orange palette, edges labeled Delta rho, rho Delta phi, rho sin phi Delta theta. Formula text rendered as an HTML/sprite overlay: Delta V = rho^2 sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta. Edge-highlight colors: radial #ff2200, polar #00aa00, azimuthal #0066ff applied to the matching edge line on both boxes when selected.
interactionPlan.notes: Rebuild the curved wedge geometry (BufferGeometry from a parametric grid) and the straightened inset box reactively on every slider change; recompute arc-edge lengths rho*dphi and rho*sin(phi)*dtheta so the inset visibly stretches along the correct axis. Keep the in-place wedge and the inset as separate groups so the edgeHighlight toggle can recolor the matching edge line on both. Render dashed arcs/rays with LineDashedMaterial and call computeLineDistances(). Use sprite or CSS2D labels for Delta rho, Delta phi, Delta theta, rho sin phi, rho sin phi Delta theta and the three inset edge labels; fade non-selected labels to ~0.25 opacity when a single edge is highlighted. The gray sweep arrow and the Delta V formula are static overlays that do not depend on slider state.

authoredContext:
Now we can illustrate the following theorem for triple integrals in spherical coordinates with (ρijk*,θijk*,φijk*) being any sample point in the spherical subbox Bijk. For the volume element of the subbox ΔV in spherical coordinates, we have ΔV=(Δρ)(ρΔφ)(ρsinφΔθ),, as shown in the following figure.

The volume element of a box in spherical coordinates.

In the spherical coordinate space, a box is projected onto the polar coordinate plane. On the polar coordinate plane, the projection has area rho sin phi Delta theta. On the z axis, a distance Delta rho is indicated, and from these boundaries, angles are made that project through the edges of the box. There is also a blown up version of the box that shows it has sides Delta rho, rho Delta phi, and rho sin phi Delta theta, with overall volume Delta V = rho squared sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta.

As with the other multiple integrals we have examined, all the properties work similarly for a triple integral in the spherical coordinate system, and so do the iterated integrals. Fubini’s theorem takes the following form.

A bracket on the z axis marks the radial increment Delta rho, the angular gap between the two rays reaching the box is marked Delta phi, and a small angle in the horizontal plane near the origin is marked Delta theta. A flat blue quadrilateral in the xy-plane is the projection of the box, with a bracket beneath labeled rho sin phi and an arrow into it labeled rho sin phi Delta theta. A thick gray curved arrow sweeps right to an enlarged copy of the same box, whose three edges are labeled Delta rho, rho Delta phi, and rho sin phi Delta theta, with Delta V = rho^2 sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta printed below. Showing the subbox in place and again blown up lets each edge be matched to the coordinate increment that generates it. The construction motivates the factor rho^2 sin phi that appears when a triple integral is rewritten in spherical coordinates.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for Delta rho, Delta phi, and Delta theta: the learner drags each increment and the orange spherical subbox plus its magnified inset stretch along the matching edge, making clear how the three coordinate increments multiply into Delta V.
- Toggle between in-place and enlarged element labels: the learner switches label overlays on the coordinate diagram and the inset, and the same edge is highlighted in both locations, making clear why rho Delta phi and rho sin phi Delta theta are arc-length factors rather than raw angle measures.
